Idea: a 40 EUR spreadsheet-automation course for office workers, built in 4 weeks at 6 h/week (about 24 h), sold via LinkedIn posts. Decision: start building.

**Verdict:** Fix first (confidence: medium, because nothing here is fatal, but demand and reach are both unproven and the build is committed before either is tested)
**If you only do one thing:** Post on LinkedIn today (30 min) naming one specific, painful spreadsheet task. Offer a 40 EUR early-bird spot and ask people to reply "me" or pay a deposit.

**1. Free and AI substitutes may make "automation for office workers" a hard sell** (fixable)
- Why: Free tutorials, vendor docs and AI assistants already explain macros, formulas and Power Query (assumption, verify: search YouTube and Udemy for your exact topic). A generic course gives buyers no reason to pay.
- Test: At least 10 of the people who see your posts will pay or leave a deposit for one named workflow within 14 days | pass if 10 or more.
- If true: Narrow to one role and one outcome, such as "monthly finance report in 10 minutes", and sell the result rather than the tool.

**2. LinkedIn posts alone may not reach enough buyers** (fixable)
- Why: Your audience size and its fit with office workers are not stated (unchecked). Even a good post reaches only a small share of followers (assumption, verify in your own analytics). Buyers are also hard to reach while at work.
- Test: At least 3 % of the people who read 4 posts over 2 weeks will click to a waitlist page | pass if 3 % or more; below 1 % means the channel or message needs changing.
- If true: Add a second channel (an employer's training budget, a spreadsheet community, or direct outreach to team leads) before building.

**3. 24 hours is likely too little for building and promoting a course** (fixable)
- Why: Recording, editing, exercises and a sales page usually take many times the finished course length (assumption, verify). The 6 h/week does not clearly include writing posts or answering buyers.
- Test: Build and record lesson 1 (about 10 minutes) in 3 h or less | pass if it is done and usable.
- If true: Cut the scope to one 60-minute core course with templates, and set aside 2 of the 6 weekly hours for promotion.

**Strongest case for the idea:** 40 EUR is a low-risk price, spreadsheet time-savers are a daily pain, and an employee can easily pay for one on their own or expense it.
**Would change my mind:** 10 or more paying or deposit-leaving buyers from posts before you record anything, or 3 % or more waitlist clicks.

*Prior rating/claims not verified: your confidence in the idea and the 4-week plan rest on no stated evidence, so I treated demand as E0 (opinion) and planned timing as unmeasured. Assumed: solo creator, no sales or audience data yet, about 24 h at stake plus reputation. Next step: `idea-to-plan` to build the tests into a plan, `idea-evaluation` to re-rank after results.*
